title: Research: audit PR #3128's retained aliases across scatter guards and native COPY counts (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Add `research/scatter-alias-native-audit`, a bounded independent native-boundary audit of PR #3128's retained-helper aliases on the selected PR #589 bit word. The balanced alias appends helper 480 as retained slot 9 and `[8,8,9,9]` to scatter row 64. It passes actual legality and all 883 five-stage formal columns with `NCOPY=10`; the selected `NCOPY=9` builds reject it. Its complete local invoice retains the extra rank-seven COPY/ERASE pair and two ADDs: rank mass 5,129→5,136, records 27,234→27,238. Five-stage ADDs rise by ten and fresh copies by five; the 93-bit prefix bound is unchanged.

A new unused-slot positive control leaves scatter rows unchanged. Both real simple-scatter entry points accept it, while the selected native copy-count contract rejects it. Thus the guard enforces row support, not retained-list injectivity or the selected COPY count. It correctly rejects the three repeated-row fixtures before output creation and preserves existing artifacts.

This is finite audit evidence, not supplier admission or a new kappa. Frozen inputs, shared code and the selected frontier are unchanged. Physical bank/projector/hosting admission, full nine-stage allocation and supplier moments, all-size compilation, precision/tape and analytic transfer remain unverified here.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_baseline.py
python3 -I -O -Werror -B research/scatter-export-parity-audit/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/scatter-alias-native-audit --check-only
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/scatter-alias-native-audit
python3 -I -O -Werror -B research/scatter-alias-native-audit/verify.py --native
python3 scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/scatter-alias-native-audit
```

All passed locally on CPython 3.12.3, GCC 13.3.0, Linux x86_64. Registered replay: 11.139 s; explicit native replay: 31.625 s. Observed:

```text
PASS_SELECTED_SCATTER_EXPORT_PARITY_AUDIT columns=661 changed_targets=1 no_new_kappa
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)

Ran 6 tests ... OK

PASS_SCATTER_ALIAS_NATIVE_AUDIT fixtures=5 contracts=2 native_columns=883 controls=3 no_new_kappa
PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES {"commit": "0438cf1edcda3f68dfae345db87d4d690ab95efa", "files": 23, "package": "research/scatter-alias-native-audit"}
```

`RESULT.json` and `NATIVE.json` retain deterministic receipts. Four sequential C++ builds use the pinned checked-128-bit cpp_int stand-in; the independent Python prefix calculation uses unbounded integers. Only validated time/path fields are normalized. The selected baseline exactly reproduces PR #2977's native receipts.

Six behavioral groups pass. Actual native controls distinguish an underpriced COPY (legality rejects, columns pass), a wrong ERASE source (both reject), and an omitted scatter ADD (legality passes, columns reject). Source corruption, full dirty-column controls, record alignment/lifetime failures, guard preservation and saved-invoice tampering are also checked. All 23 package/input publication-byte comparisons and staged whitespace checks pass.

The generic registered hook does not compile native code; the explicit command above does. Native staging has an empty kernel selection and no source owners/donors. Inherited bank-audit flags are not new bank verification. System Boost, full selected cold replay, hosted CI, independent human review and proof-kernel verification were not run.

## Open next questions

These fixtures provide the first bounded acceptance test; then bind the successor entry points and run its complete symbolic/export/native and bank/hosting replay. New manifests and complete supplier admission remain blockers. Changing `NCOPY` alone is not adoption. No construction search is justified by this audit. See the package README and structured `open_questions` in TASK.json.
